translation_en: Ismail narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Sa‘sa‘ah, from his father, who informed him that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri said to him: “I see that you love sheep and the desert. When you are with your sheep or in the desert and call the prayer, raise your voice in the call, for no jinn, human, or thing within the caller’s range of voice hears it except that it will testify for him on the Day of Resurrection.” Abu Sa‘id said: I heard this from the Messenger of Allah.
Qabisah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from his mother, from Aishah, who said: The Prophet used to recite the Quran while his head was in my lap and I was menstruating.

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us: Uqayl narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab: Urwah narrated to me that al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd al-Qari told him that they heard Umar ibn al-Khattab say: I heard Hisham ibn Hakim reciting Surat al-Furqan during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah. I listened to his recitation and found him reciting in many forms that the Messenger of Allah had not taught me. I was about to attack him during the prayer, but I restrained myself until he finished. Then I seized him by his cloak and said, “Who taught you this surah that I heard you reciting?” He said, “The Messenger of Allah taught it to me.” I said, “You are lying; he taught it to me differently from the way you recited it.” I took him to the Messenger of Allah and said, “I heard this man reciting Surat al-Furqan in forms you did not teach me.” He said, “Let him go. Recite, Hisham.” He recited the way I had heard him. The Messenger of Allah said, “Thus it was revealed.” Then he said, “Recite, Umar.” I recited the way he had taught me. He said, “Thus it was revealed. This Quran was revealed in seven forms, so recite whatever is easy for you.”

Abu Ma‘mar narrated to us: Abd al-Warith narrated to us: Yazid said: Mutarrif ibn Abdullah narrated to me, from Imran, who said: I asked, “Messenger of Allah, what are people doing deeds for?” He said, “Everyone is facilitated toward that for which he was created.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to me: Ghundar narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Mansur and al-A‘mash, who heard Sa‘d ibn Ubaydah, from Abu Abd al-Rahman, from Ali, from the Prophet, who was at a funeral, took a stick, and began scratching the ground with it. He said, “There is none of you whose place has not been written, either in the Fire or in Paradise.” They said, “Should we not then rely on that?” He said, “Act, for everyone is facilitated,” then recited, “As for him who gives and is mindful of Allah…” Quran 92:5, through the verse.

Khalifah ibn Khayyat said to me: Mu‘tamir narrated to us: I heard my father narrate, from Qatadah, from Abu Rafi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet, who said: “When Allah completed creation, He wrote a writing with Him: ‘My mercy prevails over’”—or he said, “has preceded”—“My anger. It is with Him above the Throne.”

Muhammad ibn Abi Ghalib narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Ismail narrated to us: Mu‘tamir narrated to us: I heard my father say: Qatadah narrated to us, that Abu Rafi narrated to him that he heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say, “Allah wrote a writing before He created creation: ‘My mercy preceded My anger.’ It is written with Him above the Throne.”

Abdullah ibn Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Abu Qilabah and al-Qasim al-Tamimi, from Zahdam, who said: There were bonds of affection and brotherhood between this clan of Jurm and the Ash‘aris. We were with Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari when food containing chicken was brought to him. A man from Banu Taym Allah was with him, appearing to be a freedman. Abu Musa invited him to eat, but he said, “I saw it eating something and found it repulsive, so I swore that I would not eat it.” Abu Musa said, “Come here, and I will tell you about that. I came to the Prophet with a group of Ash‘aris to ask him for mounts. He said, ‘By Allah, I will not give you mounts; I have nothing on which to carry you.’ Then some camels taken as spoils were brought to the Prophet, and he asked about us, saying, ‘Where are the Ash‘ari men?’ He ordered that we be given five young, fine camels. We set out and said, ‘What have we done? The Messenger of Allah swore he would not give us mounts and said he had nothing to carry us, then he gave us mounts. We took the Messenger of Allah unawares with respect to his oath. By Allah, we will never prosper.’ We returned to him and told him. He said, ‘I am not the one who gave you mounts; Allah gave you mounts. By Allah, I never swear an oath and then see something better than it without doing what is better and making expiation for my oath.’”

Amr ibn Ali narrated to us: Abu Asim narrated to us: Qurrah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Abu Jamrah al-Duba‘i narrated to us: I said to Ibn Abbas: The delegation of Abd al-Qays came to the Messenger of Allah and said, “Between us and you are the polytheists of Mudar, and we can come to you only during the sacred months. Give us concise instructions which, if we act upon them, will admit us to Paradise and which we can invite those behind us to follow.” He said, “I command you to do four things and forbid you from four. I command you to believe in Allah. Do you know what belief in Allah is? It is to testify that there is no god but Allah, establish prayer, give zakat, and give one fifth of the spoils. I forbid you from four things: do not drink from the gourd, the hollowed log, the pitch-coated vessels, or the green jar.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: al-Layth narrated to us, from Nafi, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aishah, that the Messenger of Allah said, “The makers of these images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them, ‘Bring to life what you created.’”

Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us, from Ayyub, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Prophet said, “The makers of these images will be punished on the Day of Resurrection, and it will be said to them, ‘Bring to life what you created.’”

Muhammad ibn al-Ala narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Umārah, from Abu Zur‘ah, who heard Abu Hurayrah say: I heard the Prophet say: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says, ‘Who is more unjust than one who goes to create as I create? Let them create an atom, or a grain, or a barley grain.’”

Hudbah ibn Khalid narrated to us: Hammam narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us: Anas narrated to us, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, who said: “The likeness of the believer who recites the Quran is that of a citron: its taste is good and its fragrance is good. The believer who does not recite it is like a date: its taste is good but it has no fragrance. The likeness of the wicked person who recites the Quran is that of basil: its fragrance is good but its taste is bitter. The likeness of the wicked person who does not recite the Quran is that of a colocynth: its taste is bitter and it has no fragrance.”

Ali narrated to us: Hisham narrated to us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri. Ahmad ibn Salih narrated to me: Anbasah narrated to us: Yunus narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab: Yahya ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr informed me that he heard Urwah ibn al-Zubayr say: Aishah said: Some people asked the Prophet about soothsayers. He said, “They are nothing.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, sometimes they tell something that turns out to be true.” The Prophet said, “That is a word of truth which a jinni snatches and murmurs into the ear of his ally like a hen’s clucking; then they mix more than one hundred lies into it.”

Abu al-Nu‘man narrated to us: Mahdi ibn Maymun narrated to us: I heard Muhammad ibn Sirin narrate, from Ma‘bad ibn Sirin, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet, who said: “People will emerge from the east and recite the Quran, but it will not pass beyond their throats. They will pass out of the religion as an arrow passes through its target, and they will not return to it until the arrow returns to its bow.” It was asked, “What is their distinguishing sign?” He said, “Their sign is shaving”—or he said, “having their hair cut short.”

Ahmad ibn Ishaq narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from Umārah ibn al-Qa‘qa, from Abu Zur‘ah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Prophet said, “Two words are beloved to the Most Merciful, light on the tongue and heavy on the scales: ‘Glory and praise be to Allah; glory be to Allah, the Magnificent.’”
